newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Deepening Malaysia tension hits Singapore stocks.
newsitem.headline: Deepening Malaysia tension hits Singapore stocks.

text.p: Deepening diplomatic tension with Malaysia hit Singapore shares in early Wednesday trade.
"When such political issues arise, there is always volatility in the market," a dealer with a local firm said.
The barometer Straits Times Industrials Index lost half a percent in early trade, down 13.31 at 2,098.29 at 0230 GMT.
The mainly Malaysian-share tracking UOB over-the-counter index was down 8.17 at 1,292.79 by the same point.
"This is all a bit of a let down. The market was showing signs of recovery and now this hits us," another dealer said.

The early falls, producing 209 losing issues against 26 gainers, were sparked by Malaysia's decision to freeze all new bilateral ties with Singapore following a row over criticism of a Malaysian state by Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.
"Investors are worried because the situtation is pretty ambiguous. A ban on bilateral relations could mean anything," said a concerned Singapore stock dealer.

Early losers were Asia Pacific Breweries and Creative Technology, both a dollar down at Singapore $7.00 S$13.40 respectively. Malaysia's Berjaya Leisure and Samanda Holdings were early gainers, up S$0.26 and S$0.20 at S$4.32 and S$9.20 resepectively.
